description: The fib entry with its compression replaced: the JSON routes sit behind a compression middleware written in the entry on fib's middleware API (Context.OnResponse, as fib's own compress, around the routes through Router.With), coding brotli (molecule-man/go-brrr, the encoder fasthttp and so fiber-tuned use), zstd, gzip and deflate (klauspost/compress) as Accept-Encoding weighs them, with fiber-tuned's settings (compress.LevelBestSpeed): brotli quality 0, zstd fastest, gzip and deflate level 1, bodies of 200 bytes or more, and between codings a client weighs the same brotli first, then zstd, gzip and deflate, fiber's order. JSON responses are encoded with sonic, which Context.JSON calls as fib's JSONEncoder. It runs with GOGC=200. Everything else - prefork with a child for every two CPUs, fib's default configuration, listeners on 8080/8082/8081/8443 tcp+udp/9000, fib's Router and routes, gRPC through fib's grpc package, static through FileCache, TLS - is the fib entry's.
